newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel trades lower, jet slides.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel trades lower, jet slides.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil market was swamped with offers as traders with arbitrage cargoes emerged to sell but only two buyers were seen and prices dipped on both the physical and swaps markets, traders said on Wednesday.
They said seven sellers were seen with offers between $27.20 and $28.50, down from Tuesday's traded levels of $28.20 for early April and $29.00 for second half April.
A Singapore trader pushed his total purchases to around 5.7 million barrels on Wednesday. He bought another 220,000 barrels from a European major at $27.25 per barrel for April 19-23 lifting, fob.
A Japanese trader bought 150,000 barrels from a US major at $28.50 for April 10-14 lifting fob.
Traders expect physical gas oil prices to slip by another 50 cents per barrel on Thursday.

Swaps gas oil fell on concerns that the Singapore trader who has been instrumental in supporting prices might have exhausted his run. Swaps for April lost another 20-25 cents per barrel to be last quoted at $26.25/$26.35.
Jet fuel continued to slide with an April 18-22 cargo offered at $26.30, down 50 cents from Tuesday.
Trade sources said Indonesia has sealed an annual contract with Kuwait to buy 55,000 tonnes of jet fuel to be delivered every 40 days.
The deal signalled Indonesia's aim to diversify its sources of middle-distillate supplies from Singapore.
Sri Lanka has issued a tender to buy 200,000 barrels of gas oil and 80,000 barrels of jet fuel for April 21-22 delivery delivery, closing April 1.
Taiwan is expected to issue its next jet fuel tender later
this week or early next week, source said.
